research_dossier.title: From Ṣāliḥ's rescue to Abraham's visitors (Q 11:66–70)
research_dossier.chronology: Genesis is an earlier Jewish scriptural narrative with complex composition and textual transmission. Dating of textual composition cannot be equated with the date of the medieval Hebrew codices or modern English editions. No pre-Islamic textual witness to the Ṣāliḥ rescue was established here.
research_dossier.comparative_discussion: Q 11:66–68 closes the Thamūd episode with rescue and punishment; these verses are not mapped to Abraham's Genesis episode. Q 11:69–70 begins a distinct Abraham/Lot narrative. Genesis 18:1–8 shares visitors, hospitality and calf preparation. A significant difference is that Genesis explicitly reports eating, whereas Q 11:70 makes non-eating the trigger for Abraham's fear. Q 11:70's commission against Lot's people should be studied alongside Genesis 18:16–19:3, not conflated with the hospitality passage.

research_dossier.variant_witnesses: Masoretic Hebrew, Septuagint Greek, Samaritan Pentateuch and relevant Jewish/Christian reception traditions not collated in this pass.
research_dossier.dating_caveat: Genesis literary strata, final composition, earliest attestations, and surviving manuscript dates are separate questions; this batch does not assign unsupported exact dates.
research_dossier.similarities_and_differences: Both accounts describe Abraham entertaining visitors and preparing calf; Genesis describes guests eating, Qur'an their refusal/non-participation. Qur'an presents a peace greeting and fear; Genesis adds footwashing, bread, milk and a detailed hospitality scene.
research_dossier.scholarly_interpretations: The common narrative can be described as a shared Abrahamic tradition, without concluding textual borrowing or specifying an unverified intermediary.
